plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and cure the mandate breach.
Reduce SMH to 8% and QQQI to 15% due to their downtrends and trim flags.
Buy SNOW at 5% as a top-quality long setup to add diversification.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and trimming concentrated positions. Expect lower drawdowns but also more modest growth potential.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 1% to keep leveraged exposure small.
Reduce SPY to 25% to address concentration and meet mandate limits.
Trim SMH to 10% and QQQI to 15% due to their downtrends and trim flags.
Buy SNOW at 4% to add a quality long setup to the portfolio.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining a diversified approach.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for approximately 2.5% per month, prioritizing risk-first growth. It reduces overall concentration and leverage while adding a quality growth name. Expect moderate drawdowns with a focus on sustainable growth.

plan: Add to SOXL and SPAL, targeting 6% each, to increase leveraged exposure.
Trim SPY to 25% to cure the concentration breach while maintaining broad exposure.
Reduce QQQI to 10% due to its downtrend and trim flag.
Buy SNOW at 6% as a high-scoring long setup.
Add to CRWD, targeting 18%, to press a working position.
This plan leans into leverage and concentration for higher growth potential.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware this approach carries substantially higher drawdown risk and leveraged ETFs experience daily decay.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Add to QQQI, targeting 30%, to increase income-generating exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and cure the mandate breach.
Sell SMH to zero to eliminate high-beta semiconductor exposure.
Trim CRWD to 5% to reduce exposure to a high-beta single name.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It rotates heavily into income-generating ETFs and broad index funds, cutting high-beta and leveraged positions. While aiming for reliable distributions, NAV can still fall in selloffs, and distributions are not guaranteed.
